The Jacobian can also be denoted by

to help us remember how the determinant in Equation (1) is constructed from the partial derivatives of x and y. The array of partial derivatives in Equation (1) behaves just like the derivative g′ in the single variable situation. The Jacobian measures how much the trans- formation is expanding or contracting the area around the point (u, y). Effectively, the factor  J converts the area of the differential rectangle du dy in G to match with its cor- responding differential area dx dy in R. We note that, in general, the value of the scaling factor  J depends on the point (u, y) in G. Our examples to follow will show how it scales the differential area du dy for specific transformations.
